title: Price Tags and Totals
goal: I can find the total cost when things have the same price.

card.desc: Bristol uses the detective questions on money stories: same price for many things (multiply), different things bought together (add), and comparing costs (subtract). She skip counts $5 and $10 bills and learns the words price, total, factor, product and multiple. This covers the main Pathways Week 7 Math skills (skip counting $5 and $10, price × how many, the shop words). She retakes Pathways Week 7 Math after Thursday. This lesson also adds add and compare money stories.

win: Great shopping! You found every total like a pro!

slides.title: Shop Practice
slides.text: You ran the pet shop with Jonathan. Now find the totals on your own! 🏷️

slides.title: Money detective
slides.text: Ask: is it the same price for each thing?

steps.text: ✖️ Same price, many things → multiply. 3 balls at $5 each: 3 × 5 = $15

slides.tip: The price is for one. The total is for all.

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say these out loud. You can tell your mom!
prompts: Read this tag three ways: 🦴 $6 each.
Tell a shop story where you multiply.

items.q: Toy balls cost $5 each. Liz buys 9. What is the total?
items.no: Each ball is $5. Skip count by 5, 9 times.
items.hint: Count 9 jumps of 5 on your fingers.

items.q: Ellie has 8 ten-dollar bills. How much money is that?
items.no: Each bill is $10. Skip count by 10s.

items.q: Marion counts her $5 bills: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. How many bills does she have?
items.why: Count the numbers, not the last one. There are 7.
items.no: Each number you say is one bill. Count the numbers.
items.hint: Touch each number as you count: 5 is one, 10 is two …

items.q: Brushes cost $4 each. Amy buys 7. What is the total?
items.no: Every brush is $4. Multiply. Then check your math.

items.q: Fish nets are $9 each. Liz buys 3. What is the total?
items.no: Every net is $9. Multiply. Then check your math.

slides.title: Multiply, add or subtract?
slides.text: Tap a money story. Then tap the right box.

items.hint: Does every hat cost the same?

items.text: A rope is $7 and a ball is $5. Buy both.

items.hint: Does Amy get money or spend it?

items.text: Every pack of seeds is $6. Liz buys 4.
A tank is $25. A net is $8. How much more is the tank?
Marion buys a $12 cage and a $9 bowl.
items.hint: Is it many things at one price?

slides.done: Same price ✖️. Different things ➕. Spend or compare ➖.

items.q: Bows are $3 each. The $3 is the ____.
items.why: The price is what one bow costs.
items.no: What one thing costs is the …

items.why: The answer when you multiply is the product.
items.no: The answer to a multiplication is the …
items.hint: It starts with p and ends with t: p _ _ _ _ _ t

items.q: Ellie pays $14 for all her things. The $14 is the ____.
items.why: The whole amount for all of it is the total.
items.no: The whole amount, all put together, is the …

items.q: Amy buys 4 bows at $5 each. Liz buys 2 hats at $9 each. Who spends more?
no: Liz spends 2 × 9 = $18. Find Amy's total: 4 × 5.
Find both totals. Are $20 and $18 the same?

items.q: A bed costs $17. A blanket costs $9. How much more is the bed?
items.no: How much more means subtract. Then check your math.

items.why: 6 × 9 = 54. Check: 10 sixes is 60. Take away one 6: 54. ✔
items.hint: 10 sixes is 60. Take away one 6: 54. How many sixes is that?

sets.q: Leashes cost $9 each. Ellie buys 5. What is the total?
sets.no: Every leash is $9. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: A bowl costs $6. A brush costs $8. Liz buys one of each. What does she pay?
sets.no: Two different things. Do they join? Then check your math.

sets.q: Marion has 7 ten-dollar bills. How much money is that?
sets.no: Each bill is $10. Skip count by 10s.

sets.q: Bags of seed cost $4 each. The club buys 7 bags. Which number sentence finds the total?
no: Every bag costs $4. That is multiply.
The price is $4, not $7.

sets.q: A cage is $18. A bed is $9. How much more is the cage?
sets.no: How much more means subtract. Then check your math.

sets.q: Amy buys 2 brushes at $8 each. Ellie buys 3 combs at $6 each. Who spends more?
no: Amy spends 2 × 8 = $16. Find Ellie's total: 3 × 6.
Find both totals. Are $16 and $18 the same?

sets.q: In 6 × $5 = $30, what is the product?
sets.why: The product is the answer when you multiply: 30.
sets.no: The product is the answer after the = sign.

sets.q: Which number is a multiple of 5?
sets.why: Skip count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, … 40, 45. You land on 45.
no: 32 ends in 2. Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5.
54 ends in 4. Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5.

sets.q: Bird toys cost $7 each. Liz buys 6. What is the total?
sets.no: Every toy is $7. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: A collar costs $9. A tag costs $7. Amy buys one of each. What does she pay?
sets.no: Two different things. Do they join? Then check your math.

sets.q: Ellie has 9 five-dollar bills. How much money is that?
sets.no: Each bill is $5. Skip count by 5s.

sets.q: Leashes cost $8 each. Marion buys 3. Which number sentence finds the total?
no: Every leash costs $8. That is multiply.
She buys 3 leashes, not 8.

sets.q: A cat tree is $21. A cat bed is $13. How much more is the cat tree?
sets.no: How much more means subtract. Then check your math.

sets.q: Liz buys 3 balls at $5 each. Ellie buys 2 ropes at $8 each. Who spends more?
no: Liz spends 3 × 5 = $15. Find Ellie's total: 2 × 8.
Find both totals. Are $15 and $16 the same?

sets.q: In 8 × $3 = $24, what is the product?
sets.why: The product is the answer when you multiply: 24.
sets.no: The product is the answer after the = sign.

sets.q: Which number is a multiple of 10?
sets.why: Skip count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. You land on 50.
no: 15 is a multiple of 5, not of 10.
55 is a multiple of 5, not of 10.

sets.q: Dog beds cost $8 each. The shelter buys 6. What is the total?
sets.no: Every bed is $8. Multiply. Then check your math.

sets.q: Ellie buys a bowl for $7 and a brush for $5. What does she pay?
sets.no: Two different things. Do they join? Then check your math.

sets.q: Liz has 6 ten-dollar bills. How much money is that?
sets.no: Each bill is $10. Skip count by 10s.

sets.q: Fish food costs $5 a box. Amy buys 9 boxes. Which number sentence finds the total?
no: Every box costs $5. That is multiply.
She buys 9 boxes, not 5.

sets.q: A cage is $25. A mat is $16. How much more is the cage?
sets.no: How much more means subtract. Then check your math.

sets.q: Marion buys 4 bows at $6 each. Amy buys 3 hats at $8 each. Who spends more?
sets.why: Marion: 4 × 6 = 24. Amy: 3 × 8 = 24. They spend the same.
no: Marion spends 4 × 6 = $24. Find Amy's total: 3 × 8.
Amy spends 3 × 8 = $24. Find Marion's total: 4 × 6.

sets.q: In 7 × $4 = $28, what is the product?
sets.why: The product is the answer when you multiply: 28.
sets.no: The product is the answer after the = sign.

sets.q: Liz skip counts by 5s. Which number will she land on?
no: 42 ends in 2. Skip counting by 5 lands on numbers ending in 0 or 5.
53 ends in 3. Skip counting by 5 lands on numbers ending in 0 or 5.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Find the price. Then ask: same price for each thing?

questions.q: Cat toys cost $5 each. Ellie buys 8. What is the total?
questions.no: Each toy costs $5. Skip count 8 times.

questions.q: Each leash costs $10. Amy buys 6. What is the total?
questions.no: Every leash is $10. Skip count by 10s.

questions.why: Per bag means for each bag. One bag costs $7.
no: It is the other way. Look at what comes after per.
$7 is the price of one bag, not all of them.

questions.q: Bird seed is $6 a bag. Marion buys 4 bags. What is the total?
questions.no: Each bag is $6. Multiply. Then check your math.

questions.q: A fish tank is $16. A net is $7. How much more is the tank?
questions.no: How much more means subtract. Then check your math.

questions.q: A ball is $4. A rope toy is $9. Liz buys both. What does she pay?
questions.no: The prices are different. She buys both, so add. Then check your math.

questions.q: Skip count the $5 bills: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. How many bills?
questions.no: Each number you say is one bill. Count the numbers.
questions.hint: Point to each number and count.

questions.q: Collars cost $8 each. Amy buys 6. What is the total?
no: $14 is 8 + 6. Every collar is $8.
$42 is 6 × 7. The price is $8.

questions.why: Factors are the numbers you multiply: 4 and 9.
no: 36 is the product, the answer.
36 is the product. Which two numbers do you multiply?

questions.q: Ellie has $20. She buys a brush for $8. How much money is left?
questions.no: She spends money, so subtract. Then check your math.

questions.q: Amy buys 2 bags at $9 each. Liz buys 3 bags at $6 each. Who spends more?
no: Find Liz's total too: 3 × 6.
Find Amy's total too: 2 × 9.

questions.q: Bones cost $6 each. Amy buys 9. What is the total?
questions.no: Every bone is $6. Multiply. Then check your math.

teacher.objective: Bristol finds totals in money stories: price × how many when every item costs the same, add for different items, subtract to compare costs or find what is left. She skip counts $5 and $10 bills and uses the words price, total, factor, product and multiple. Week 4 Day 2 (Practice it), aimed at the Pathways Week 7 Math retake.
materials: Play money: about 12 $5 bills, 10 $10 bills and 30 $1 bills
Index cards for price tags ($4 each, $5 each, $6 each, $10 each)
Her book, Amy and the Missing Puppy
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home
The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)

plan.do: Class slide 1. The shop is set up before she arrives. Write PRICE and HOW MANY on the whiteboard.
Class slide 2. What happened since Monday, the clue she found, what Amy should buy and why.
Class slide 3. Check Monday's After-Class score first. She says the 3 detective questions on the first item.
Class slides 4–5. She reads price tags three ways; says and spells price, total, factor, product, multiple while you write them.
Class slides 6–7. She lays one $5 bill per collar and counts aloud; then $10 bills. Bills (jumps) vs dollars (last number).
Class slides 8–9. Frame: how many × price = total. She pays for 3 toys at $6 on 3 plates. Factors and product.
Class slide 10. You are the customer. She writes each number sentence on the whiteboard before giving the total.
Class slides 11–12. Act out same price, two different things, and compare; then she names the operation for six stories.
Class slides 13–14. You model finding both totals; then she solves three shop problems on the whiteboard.
Class slide 15. Price (spelled), product, multiples of 10.
Class slide 16. Show the task list: tonight the After-Class Lesson and the Lesson 9 Practice; Wednesday this Practice, the Lesson 9 Packet and page 1 of this Packet; 10 minutes of reading each night.

watch: Adding the price and the number (5 + 7 for 7 boxes at $5). Ask: does every box cost $5? Lay down one bill per box.
Giving the last skip-count number when the question asks how many bills or jumps. Have her touch each bill as she counts.
Multiplying two different prices ($6 and $8 → 48). Ask: is it many things at the same price, or two different things?
"How much more" answered by adding. Ask: are we putting together or comparing?
Mixing up factor and product. Factors go in, the product comes out.
Facts: 8 × 6 as 42, 4 × 8 as 36. Name the strategy (double the 4s; double, double).
teacher.notes: Tonight and Wednesday are the heavy nights of the week (Monday's Practice and Packet are on this list). Packet page 2 is on Thursday's task list. Thursday (Lesson 11) is Prove it, and after it she retakes Pathways Week 7 Math with you. Keep the price tags and play money for Thursday. If she scores under 85 on the After-Class Show What You Know, start Thursday with 10 minutes of the play-money shop (same price → multiply; two different things → add; how much more → subtract) and have her retake it (she gets a new question set) before Lesson 11. Check her spelling of the five words on packet page 2; the Pathways retake asks her to type some of them.

tasks: Tuesday night: do the After-Class Lesson. Finish with Show What You Know.
Tuesday night: do the Lesson 9 Practice.
Wednesday: do the Lesson 9 Packet, pages 1 and 2.
Wednesday: do page 1 of the Lesson 10 Packet.
Wednesday: do the reading lesson Pathways Week 14 Reading: Why Did the Author Write It? Tell why the author wrote the piece. Aim for 85. If it is locked, type 1111.
Tuesday and Wednesday: read your book for 10 minutes each day.

slides.title: Price Tags and Totals
slides.text: Pretend the Critter Club has a pet shop sale. 🏷️ Today you find out what things cost!

notes.do: Before she arrives, set up the shop: 5–6 toys with index-card price tags ($4 each, $5 each, $6 each, $10 each), play money in piles by bill, 3 paper plates, whiteboard.
notes.say: "Today the Critter Club has a pet shop sale. You are the shopkeeper. You will find out what things cost."
notes.ask: "Have you ever paid for something at a store? What did you need to know?"
notes.listen: The price, how many, how much money. Write PRICE and HOW MANY on the whiteboard.

slides.title: What happened next?
slides.text: Think about Amy and the Missing Puppy.
prompts: What happened in the part you read since Monday?
What clue did you find? Tell me about it.
If Amy could buy one thing for the puppy, what should it be? Why?

notes.do: Book talk, about 6 minutes. She shows you the clue she found (Monday's reading task).
notes.ask: All three prompts. For the last one, push for a reason from the story: "Why would the puppy need that?"
notes.listen: A clue from the text and a reason with "because". If her retell jumps around, ask: "What happened first? Next?"

items.q: Liz has 16 beads. Marion has 9 beads. How many more does Liz have?
no: 25 is 16 + 9. How many more means subtract.
Check: 8 + 9 = 17, not 16. Count up from 9 to 16.

items.q:
6 × 9 = ?
Hint: 10 groups, take away one.
no: 56 is 7 × 8. Try 10 × 6 = 60, then take away 6.
63 is 7 × 9. There are 6 nines here.

items.q: Which story is equal groups?
choices: There are 6 cages with 3 birds in each.
items.why: Each cage has 3 birds. Equal groups → multiply.
no: 5 and 3 are different amounts. That is add.
She lost 2. That is subtract.

notes.do: Glance at Monday's After-Class Lesson score first. She says the 3 detective questions out loud on the first item before answering.
notes.ask: "How many more: join or compare?" "6 × 9: what is 10 × 6?" "Which story has equal groups? Prove it."
notes.listen: 7 (compare, subtract), 54, the cages. If she picks 25 on the first item, she is still number grabbing: go back to the 3 questions.

slides.title: What is a price?

steps.text: $4 each means one bone costs 4 dollars.
$4 per bone means the same thing.
$4 a bone means the same thing too!

slides.tip: each, per and a tell you every one costs the same. That is equal groups!

notes.do: Hand her a toy with a $4 tag. She reads the tag three ways: $4 each, $4 per bone, $4 a bone. Then she reads two more tags the same way.
notes.say: "The price is what ONE thing costs. Each, per and a all mean the same thing: every one costs the same."
notes.ask: "If one bone is $4, what does a second bone cost?"
notes.listen: "$4 too. They all cost the same." That is the equal-groups idea in money.

slides.title: Shop words
slides.text: Tap each card to flip it. Say the word. Then spell it out loud.

words.meaning: The whole amount, all put together.
A number you land on when you skip count.

notes.do: Flip each card. She says the word, spells it out loud, and you write it on the whiteboard as she spells. She copies price and total on an index card to keep.
notes.say: "Pathways asks you to TYPE some of these words, so spelling counts."
notes.ask: "In 3 × 5 = 15, which numbers are the factors? Which is the product?"
notes.listen: Factors 3 and 5, product 15. Watch the spellings: price (not prise), total, factor, product, multiple.

slides.title: Skip count the money
slides.text: Collars cost $5 each. Ellie buys 6 collars.

steps.text: Make one jump of 5 for each collar.
6 jumps land on 30. So 6 × 5 = 30. The total is $30.
Now $10 each. Ellie buys 4 leashes: 10, 20, 30, 40. The total is $40.

slides.tip: Each jump is one thing you buy. The last number is the total.

notes.do: Hands on. She "buys" 6 collars: she lays one $5 bill next to each collar and counts out loud 5, 10, 15 … Then 4 leashes with $10 bills.
notes.ask: "How many bills did you lay down? What did you land on?"
notes.listen: 6 bills, $30; 4 bills, $40. She must tell apart HOW MANY bills (jumps) and HOW MUCH money (last number).

items.q: Fish food costs $5 a box. Amy buys 7 boxes. What is the total?
no: $12 is 5 + 7. Each box costs $5. Skip count 7 times.
$30 is only 6 jumps. Count the boxes: 7.

items.q: Each bag of hay costs $10. The club buys 8 bags. What is the total?
no: $18 is 10 + 8. Each bag costs $10.
$70 is 7 bags. Count again: 8 bags.

items.q: Liz counts her $5 bills: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45. How many bills does she have?
items.why: Count the jumps, not the last number. There are 9 numbers, so 9 bills.
no: $45 is how much money. The question asks how many bills.
Point to each number as you count. There are 9.

notes.do: Guided practice. She reads each one aloud and counts with real bills before answering.
notes.ask: On the last item: "Does the question ask how many dollars or how many bills?"
notes.listen: $35, $80, 9 bills. If she says 45 on the last one, have her touch each number as she counts.

slides.title: Price × how many
slides.text: When every thing costs the same, multiply.

visual.sub: Price × how many works too. It is the same total!

steps.text: Toy mice cost $4 each. Marion buys 6.

slides.tip: The price and the how many are the factors. The total is the product.

notes.do: Reveal step by step. Write the frame on the whiteboard: how many × price = total. She puts $4 on each of 6 plates (use the 3 plates twice, or draw circles).
notes.say: "When every thing costs the same, we multiply. The price and the how-many are the factors. The total is the product."
notes.ask: "Which number is the price? Which is how many? What is 6 × 4? How do you know?"
notes.listen: Double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24. If she says 10, she added: point to each plate and ask what is on it.

slides.title: Ellie's dog toys
slides.text: Dog toys cost $6 each. Ellie buys 3. Make one group of $6 for each toy.
slides.hint: Make one group for each toy. Put $6 in each group.

notes.do: She pays for 3 toys at $6 with $1 bills on 3 plates, then sets the groups on screen.
notes.ask: "How many groups? How many dollars in each group? Which numbers are the factors? What is the product?"
notes.listen: 3 groups of 6, $18. Factors 3 and 6, product 18. If she makes 6 groups of 3, ask: "How many toys did you buy?"

slides.title: Shop role-play
slides.text: Your teacher is the customer. You are the shopkeeper. 🧾
prompts: "I want 4 balls. They are $5 each. What do I pay?"
"I want 7 bones. They are $4 each. What do I pay?"
"I have $10 bills. I want 5 leashes at $10 each. How many bills do I give you?"

notes.do: You play the customer with the real toys and play money. She writes each number sentence on the whiteboard before she says the total. Add one or two of your own orders if time allows.
notes.ask: After each order: "What is the price? How many? Which operation? What is the total?"
notes.listen: 4 × 5 = $20; 7 × 4 = $28 (double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28); 5 bills, $50. If she adds the price and the how-many, lay one tag on each item and ask: "Does every ball cost $5?"

slides.title: Not every money story is ✖️

steps.text: ✖️ Same price, many things. 5 bowls at $3 each → 5 × 3 = $15
➕ Different things together. A leash is $9. A collar is $6. Buy both → 9 + 6 = $15
➖ Compare costs. A bed is $12. A blanket is $7. How much more is the bed? 12 − 7 = $5

slides.tip: Is it the same price for each thing? Then multiply. If not, add or compare.

notes.do: Reveal one step at a time. Act each one out with the toys: two of the same toy (multiply), two different toys (add), hold up two toys side by side (compare).
notes.say: "Money stories still need the detective questions. Not every money story is multiply."
notes.ask: "A leash is $9 and a collar is $6. Is that the same price for each thing?"
notes.listen: "No, they are different things, so add." For the bed and blanket: "how much more" means compare, so subtract.

slides.title: Multiply, add or subtract?
slides.text: Read the story. Say what is happening. Then name the operation.

items.q:
4 brushes at $5 each. What is the total?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.no: Does every brush cost the same?

items.q:
A ball is $3 and a rope toy is $8. What do both cost?
Add, subtract or multiply?

A cage is $20. A bed is $14. How much more is the cage?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.no: This asks you to compare two prices.

items.q:
Liz has $15. She spends $6. How much is left?
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.why: She spends money, so it goes away. 15 − 6.
items.no: Does Liz get money or spend it?

items.q:
Every bag of treats is $7. Amy buys 3 bags.
Add, subtract or multiply?

Ellie buys a $10 net and a $5 bowl.
Add, subtract or multiply?
items.why: Two different things, two different prices. 10 + 5.
items.no: Is it many things at the same price?

notes.do: She reads each money story aloud, names the operation, then types it on your laptop herself (spelling counts). On the whiteboard, keep three columns: ✖️ same price, ➕ different things, ➖ spend or compare, and write each story's number sentence in its column.
notes.ask: "Is it the same price for each thing? Are two different things joining? Is money spent or compared?"
notes.listen: Watch the spend story (Liz has $15, spends $6): subtract, because money goes away.

slides.title: Who spends more?
slides.text: Ellie buys 3 leashes at $6 each. Marion buys 4 collars at $4 each. Who spends more?

steps.text: Compare: $18 is more than $16. Ellie spends more. 18 − 16 = $2 more.

notes.do: Model it on the whiteboard: two boxes, one for each girl. Find each total, then compare. Then let her lay out the money for each girl to prove it.
notes.say: "The girl with more things does not always spend more. We have to find both totals."
notes.ask: Before revealing: "Who do you think spends more? Why?" After: "How much more?"
notes.listen: Ellie, $2 more. If she guesses Marion because Marion buys more things, point to both totals: Ellie buys fewer things but spends more.

items.q: Collars cost $8 each. Marion buys 4. What is the total?
no: $12 is 8 + 4. She buys 4 collars at $8 each.
$36 is 4 × 9. The price is $8.

items.q: A dog bed costs $15. A cat bed costs $9. How much more is the dog bed?
no: $24 is 15 + 9. How much more means subtract.
Check: 5 + 9 = 14, not 15.

items.q: Amy buys 3 bags of food at $7 each. Liz buys 4 toys at $5 each. Who spends more?
no: Liz spends 4 × 5 = $20. Now find Amy's total: 3 × 7.
Find both totals. Are $21 and $20 the same?

notes.do: Guided practice. She solves each one on the whiteboard first, then answers. She says the operation out loud before the total.
notes.ask: "Same price, different things, or compare?" On the last one: "What are both totals?"

items.q:
Bones are $4 each. Ellie buys 7. She pays $28.
The $4 is the ____.
items.no: What does one bone cost? What is that called?

items.q: In 7 × $5 = $35, what is the product?
items.why: The product is the answer when you multiply: 35.
items.no: The product is the answer after the = sign.

items.q: Which numbers are all multiples of 10?
items.why: Skip count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. You land on 30, 50 and 70.
no: 25 is a multiple of 5, but not of 10.
5 is not a multiple of 10.

notes.do: Quick check for understanding. She answers out loud and spells the word. You type what she says.
notes.ask: "Spell price." "What do we call the answer to a multiplication?" "Skip count by 10s and tell me which list you land on."
notes.listen: price (spelled right), 35, the second list. If she misses the word, go back to the vocab cards (class slide 5).

slides.title: Tell me what you learned
prompts: When do you multiply in a money story?
What is the price? What is the total?
starters: The price is … The total is …

notes.do: Show the task list on the course page. Walk through it with her: tonight and Wednesday.
notes.say: "Tonight: the After-Class Lesson and Monday's Practice. Wednesday: today's Practice, Monday's Packet and page 1 of today's Packet. Read 10 minutes each night."
notes.listen: Same price for every thing → multiply. Price = one thing; total = all of it.
